content:
maria: quick sync — the new 13B candidate (open-13b-v2) shows a strange accuracy cliff after awq->gptq hybrid on some prompts. running per-layer probes now.

dave: cliff as in lamping regs or coherent collapse? any sample?

maria: coherence okay mostly but factuality scores drop on longform QAs. eval harness: exact-match down 2.4% on custom SQuAD-ish set at 512 tokens; perplexity +1.8%. happens when we quantize attention proj in layers 8..10.

li: that's the usual mid-layer attention proj outliers. did you try per-head max magnitude scan?

maria: yeah pulled per-head stats across 5k eval examples. found 2 heads in layer 9 with heavy tails (max abs > 180x median). looks like a tiny set of channels are dominating activations.

jen: can you paste the probe script? quick check to reproduce locally.

maria:
```
# per-head peak probe (snippet)
for layer in model.layers:
  for head in layer.attn.heads:
    peaks = np.max(np.abs(head.kv_activations), axis=(0,1))
    stats[layer.idx][head.idx] = np.percentile(peaks, [50,95,99,100])
```

maria: 95->100 gap > 40x for the two heads.

alex: what did AWQ/GPTQ config look like? symmetric, per-channel scale?

maria: AWQ for first-pass (4-bit, per-tensor scale), then GPTQ refinement with 128-sample second pass. didn't enable per-channel clipping.

li: ok that explains it. per-channel scaling + surgical clamp on outliers usually fixes head-wise domination. propose approaches: 1) head clamp (clip top 0.5% activations), 2) skip-quantize those two heads (keep fp16), 3) per-channel rescale (compute scale on trimmed quantiles).

jen: runbook idea: auto-detect heads with 95->100 gap > 10x -> create skiplist entry and re-run gptq on remaining weights. then eval diff. low-risk rollout if delta < 0.5% em.

maria: ran quick ablation:
- base AWQ->GPTQ: EM -2.4%
- clamp top 0.5% activations at layer9.h3/h7: EM -0.9%
- skip quantize layer9.h3 & layer9.h7 (fp16 kept): EM -0.3%
- per-channel rescale (trim 99th pct): EM -0.5%

maria: CPU perf impact: skiplist adds ~0.8% token latency (model split exec path) but reduces reg.

alex: interesting — so skiplist is best accuracy tradeoff, clamp cheaper but slightly worse.

li: question: is skiplist portable across runtimes (hosted vs dedicated)? keep an eye on kernel path mismatch. we should tag metadata: skiplist:true, reason:activation-outlier, heads:[9.3,9.7].

jen: can we try a hybrid: keep skiplist for inference at 2048 tokens for high-SLO routes, clamp for low-cost routes? routing policy could pick variant.

maria: yes — that was our internal thought. two deployment profiles:
- high-quality (dedicated/private): skiplist variant (fp16 for those heads)
- cost-optimized (hosted default): clamp variant + smaller beam chorus

auto-bakebot: upload artifact 20240308-13b-v2-probes.json -> checksums OK, fixture id bake-1134.

dave: want to run cross-seed stability? sometimes these outliers flip heads across random init seeds of calibration set.

maria: will run 3 seeds and attach diffs. also running a short canary on dedicated with traffic split 1% (skiplist) vs 99% (current groomed AWQ) — metrics to watch: EM, PPL, token-99th latency, and error-rate (invalid tokens).

li: curious about automation: let's add a job to the quant-bake repo that emits a patch skiplist if the head-gap > threshold and EM regression improves > 0.2%. PR can be auto-generated but needs human review for rollout decision.

jen: agreed. add a console flag to show "active-skiplist" in rollout metadata and surface in per-route dashboards.

maria: next steps: 1) run 3-seed stability (ETA 2h), 2) create skiplist PR if stable, 3) schedule 1% canary on dedicated in the afternoon. tagging @eng-platform for rollout knobs.

alex: thanks — ping me if you want me to help with the canary harness and analytics.

maria: will do. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
